t: A National Preserve in Alaska shall be administered and managed as a unit of the National Park System in the same manner as a national park except as otherwise provided in this Act and except that the taking of fish and wildlife for sport purposes and subsistence uses, and trapping shall be allowed in a national preserve under applicable State and Federal law and regulation. Consistent with the provisions of section 816, within national preserves the Secretary may designate zones where and periods when no hunting, fishing, trapping, or entry may be permitted for reasons of public safety, administration, floral and faunal protection, or public use and enjoyment. Except in emergencies, any regulations prescribing such restrictions relating to hunting, fishing, or trapping shall be put into effect only after consultation with the appropriate State agency having responsibility over hunting, fishing, and trapping activities.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that this is only an internal management provision for National Park System units, with the Secretary acting alone. But except in emergencies, the Secretary must consult the appropriate State agency before putting hunting, fishing, or trapping restrictions into effect. A State agency is outside the federal government, and the consultation comes before a federal regulatory decision, so this is participation.
fable.s: any regulations prescribing such restrictions relating to hunting, fishing, or trapping shall be put into effect only after consultation with the appropriate State agency having responsibility over hunting, fishing, and trapping activities

opus.w: Except in emergencies, the Secretary must consult the State agency responsible for hunting, fishing and trapping before putting these restrictions into effect. A State agency is outside the federal government, so this consultation crosses the federal boundary. The section also involves rulemaking. It is not a case of the Secretary acting alone or coordinating only with other federal officials.
opus.s: Except in emergencies, any regulations prescribing such restrictions relating to hunting, fishing, or trapping shall be put into effect only after consultation with the appropriate State agency having responsibility over hunting, fishing, and trapping activities.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to consult with a State agency before implementing regulations regarding hunting, fishing, or trapping restrictions. Since State agencies are outside the federal government, this consultation constitutes participation as defined. The requirement is mandatory ('shall be put into effect only after consultation'), satisfying the condition for 'require participation'.
qwen_chat.s: Except in emergencies, any regulations prescribing such restrictions relating to hunting, fishing, or trapping shall be put into effect only after consultation with the appropriate State agency having responsibility over hunting, fishing, and trapping activities.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "consultation with the appropriate State agency" is merely intra-governmental coordination if the State agency is considered part of the broader public sector, or that it is just a procedural formality. However, the definition explicitly states that states are OUTSIDE the federal government. Therefore, consultation with a state agency before a federal decision (implementing regulations) constitutes participation.
